annotations.title: Record what you did, so it can be checked later

description: Call this AFTER you have paid an address or called a tool, to put what you did on the record. Until now this platform answered "should I" and never heard what happened, which is the difference between a lookup and a control layer: a receipt lets the next question about this subject be asked against a record instead of a guess, and lets a verdict we gave be read back against what followed. `reference` is YOUR evidence, a transaction hash or the digest of a signed payload, and we store it WITHOUT verifying it. It comes back `claimed` and within the hour is judged against the payments we read from the chain: verified, contradicted, not found after two days, or unverifiable. Read the outcome at GET /v1/receipts/{id}. A claim never raises an evidence status, so a receipt nobody has checked never looks like one that settled. Needs a key; a receipt is readable only by the key that wrote it. WHY readOnlyHint IS false: this call writes a row in our store on behalf of the caller, so a second identical call is not free of consequence.

action.description: Which kind of thing you are recording: `payment` for money that left, `tool_call` for a call you made. It decides nothing about verification — both are stored as YOUR claim, with your `reference` as the evidence — but it decides what the receipt can later be reconciled against, and a payment filed as a tool call will never meet the chain reading that would confirm it.

amountUsd.description: What you committed, in US dollars.

chain.description: The chain it settled on, where it settled on one.

deadline.description: ISO 8601 time you expected it by. A time already past is refused, because it is usually seconds where milliseconds were meant.

expected.description: What you expected to follow, in your words. Ours to store and yours to claim.

policy.description: The policy you evaluated under, so a later disagreement can be read against what we said at the time.

reference.description: Your evidence that it happened: a transaction hash, or the digest of a signed payload. Stored, not verified.

verdict.description: The decision we gave you before you acted, for the same reason.

name: record_receipt

id.description: The receipt, for asking about it later.

meta.description: How current this answer is and what it was read from: `freshness` and the ages behind it. Present on every answer from this server, whatever the tool.

outcome.description: Always null here: the receipt is a claim when it is written. Within the hour it is judged against the payments we read from the chain; read the outcome with `receipt_status`.

recordedAt.description: When we wrote it down. Not when your action happened.

says.description: What was and was not verified.

subject.description: The address the receipt is about, read back, so a receipt cannot be filed against the wrong party.

warnings.description: Anything the server wants a caller to know about THIS answer before acting on it. Empty is the normal case and is not a guarantee.

title: Record what you did, so it can be checked later
